cases.customer_question: Can a new qualification registration proceed when the referenced module contains legacy consistency-check findings inherited from an older qualification?
question_variants: Do inherited consistency check issues block registration?
Can a new listing reuse a module with consistency warnings?
Are legacy inter-layer dependency findings acceptable?
Will consistency check findings prevent qualification?
Can old QDID consistency issues be inherited?
cases.actual_issue: A referenced module contains inter-layer consistency findings detected by current consistency-check rules, and the concern is whether those findings prevent a new qualification registration based on that module.
cases.plain_english_explanation: Older qualified designs may contain relationships that trigger warnings under newer consistency-check rules. In some cases these findings are inherited from the original qualification and do not prevent reuse of the design. The new registrant must understand that the inherited findings remain associated with the reused design.
cases.consultant_answer: Current consistency-check rules detected several inter-layer consistency conditions in the referenced module. However, these findings originated from a previously qualified design under an earlier qualification regime. The consultant concluded that new registration based on the module remained permissible, although the new registration would inherit the same consistency findings.
cases.decision_logic: The detected findings were inherited from an existing qualified design rather than introduced by the new product implementation. Because reuse of the qualified module remained permitted, the inherited consistency findings did not prevent registration.
cases.final_recommendation: Document and communicate inherited consistency-check findings to the applicant, then proceed with qualification using the referenced design if design reuse remains allowed.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Misinterpreting inherited consistency findings as a qualification blocker may cause unnecessary redesign work, qualification delays, or abandonment of a valid design-reuse path.
